rows.why: No tilt in the label, which is the text's own pairing (Gen 18:19, Jer 22:3, Ps 33:5, Amos 5:24). The problem is the example set: two of the four shown (Rom 5:16, Acts 24:25) are Greek verses where the companion is 'judgment' (krima), not justice. Rom 5:16 is a justification/condemnation verse, so a Reformed or Lutheran reader meets the justification debate inside a row about social justice, and a Jewish or secular reader sees the Hebrew pairing misrepresented as a Greek one.
rows.fix: Show Gen 18:19, Jer 22:3, Amos 5:24 and Ps 33:5 as the four examples. Move Rom 5:16 out of this row (to 'Righteousness, deliverance and life' with Rom 5:17-18, or to the justification section). Keep Acts 24:25 and John 16:8 only if the label becomes 'Righteousness and justice or judgment'.

rows.why: 1 Kgs 3:6 and Prov 16:12 show the throne and righteousness together, and no tradition objects. The row is thin because Ps 89:14 and Ps 97:2, the 'foundation of Your throne' verses, are not in it (see missing).

rows.row: The righteousness of the LORD, of God
rows.why: The note is balanced: 'God's own, or one given' is acceptable to Lutheran, Reformed and Catholic readers alike. The row, though, is filled by the word God occurring in the verse and not by the genitive 'righteousness of God'. That puts in it verses that are not about God's righteousness at all, and a Jewish or secular reader will see the label as stretched over Israel's own righteousness being denied (Deut 9:4, 9:6). The first-match order also pulls the main faith verses (Rom 1:17, 3:22, Phil 3:9, 10:3, and Rom 4:6) out of the faith row, so Rom 4 is split across two rows. That is probably why the note is needed, but Rom 1:17 is now only here and not beside 'faith'.
rows.fix: Move 1 John 3:10, Deut 9:4, Deut 9:6 and Isa 48:1 out of this row (they are 'of God' = 'from God', or deny Israel's own righteousness) into 'Do righteousness' and 'Righteousness and sin'. Keep the note as it is. Add a one-line cross-note: 'Rom 1:17, 3:22 and Phil 3:9 also speak of faith, see Righteousness and faith.' Better still, allow a verse with two companions to appear in both rows (as 1 John 3:7 already does across noun and adjective sections).

rows.why: The row puts two quite different things under one label: Paul's 'credited as righteousness through faith' (Gen 15:6, Rom 4, Gal 3:6) and pastoral virtue lists where faith is simply one of several things to pursue (1 Tim 6:11, 2 Tim 2:22). Lutheran and Reformed readers would not accept the virtue lists as 'justifying faith', and a Catholic or Wesleyan reader reading the row as 'faith produces righteousness' would be reading a claim the virtue lists do not make. Acts 17:31 is a plain misfit. The row also sits ahead of the law row, which is the known sensitive order.
rows.fix: Remove Acts 17:31. Move 1 Tim 6:11 and 2 Tim 2:22 into 'Seek, pursue, hunger for it' (they say 'pursue righteousness'), keeping Rom 9:30 here by exception. Keep Gen 15:6 as the lead. Place a combined row 'Righteousness, faith and the law in one verse' (Rom 3:21-22, 9:30-32, 10:4-6, Gal 3:6-11, Phil 3:9) before both this row and the law row so that neither tradition's text is hidden by first-match order.

rows.why: The label is neutral and the four examples fit. The order is the issue: faith is shown first, then law, so every verse containing both (Rom 10:4-6, Gal 3:21-24) is already placed under faith. A Jewish reader of the Hebrew Bible would see Paul's counterfactuals (Gal 2:21, 3:21) as the entire answer on law and righteousness, with Ps 119 as a single token and Deut 6:25 ('it will be our righteousness if we are careful to do all this commandment') absent because 'commandment' is not a companion. A Reformed reader would expect law before gospel; a Lutheran likewise.
rows.fix: Put the combined faith-and-law row first (see the faith row), then this row. Add 'commandment/statutes/ordinances' as companions of the law row so Deut 6:25, Deut 4:8 and Ps 119 verses are caught (Ps 119:7, 62, 75, 138, 160, 172 mention righteous judgments or commandments).

rows.why: The label says 'seek, pursue, hunger'. Matt 5:10 ('persecuted because of righteousness') is none of these, and Prov 11:19 is about pursuing evil. The clearest 'pursue righteousness' verses (1 Tim 6:11, 2 Tim 2:22, Rom 9:30) are in the faith row. A Reformed or Lutheran reader seeing a short row of 'pursue it' might read it as works-righteousness, when the best texts that would show Rom 9:30-31 (pursued and did not attain) and Prov 15:9/21:21 are not shown as examples.
rows.fix: Replace the examples with Matt 5:6, Matt 6:33, Prov 15:9 and Prov 21:21. Move Matt 5:10 and Prov 11:19 out (Matt 5:10 to the 'Righteousness and sin' or a persecuted row; Prov 11:19 to 'deliverance and life'). Bring in 1 Tim 6:11, 2 Tim 2:22 and Rom 9:30.

rows.why: Practice or do righteousness is the text's own phrase (1 John 2:29, 3:7; Matt 6:1; Acts 10:35). Reformed and Lutheran readers may find the row blunt, but the verses are only what they say and the justified-by-faith/works rows carry their own note. 1 Kgs 8:32 is the one weak example, since the 'doing' is God's act of judging, not human practice.
rows.fix: Optional: show Matt 6:1 in place of 1 Kgs 8:32 as the fourth example.

rows.why: No tradition objects to the pairing (Isa 64:6, Rom 6). But at least two examples do not contain 'sin' at all: 2 Cor 6:14 has anomia (lawlessness, translated 'wickedness') and Deut 9:5 has rish'ah (wickedness). The label therefore treats three different words as one. Wesleyan readers would also find Rom 6:18-20 here but not Rom 8:4, which sits under law.
rows.fix: Relabel 'Righteousness against sin and wickedness', or move the 'wickedness' verses to a separate row. Keep 1 Pet 2:24, Rom 6:16-20, Isa 64:6 and Dan 9:16 as examples.

rows.why: The Isaiah examples show exactly what the label says (46:13, 51:6, 51:8, 59:16), and no tradition owns the pairing. It is neutral between a God-given reading and a covenant-faithfulness reading.

Only 1 Sam 26:23 and Ps 143:1 contain 'faithfulness' (emunah). Ps 103:17 and Hos 10:12 have 'loving devotion' (chesed), and Zech 8:8 has 'truth' (emet). That is three words under one label, and the label also leaves out the obvious Greek pistis (faith/faithfulness) from the neighbouring faith row. No tradition is tilted, but the label overclaims.
rows.fix: Relabel 'Righteousness, loving devotion and faithfulness' and show the three Hebrew words in the row note, or split the chesed verses from the emunah/emet verses.

rows.why: Isa 32:17, 48:18, 60:17 and Heb 7:2 all show it directly. Ps 85:10 ('righteousness and peace kiss each other') is the best-known case and is missing.

Examples fit (Ezek 14:14, 14:20, Prov 11:4, Rom 5:17). Rom 5:17 ('the gift of righteousness') touches the imputed-versus-infused question, but the row only places 'gift' beside 'life' and does not say how the gift is given.
All four examples contain way, path or ways (Prov 16:31, Acts 13:10, 2 Pet 2:21, Ps 5:8) and the label is plain. Ps 23:3 ('paths of righteousness') is missing.

The label names 'the wicked' but the companions are several Hebrew and Greek words: rasha (wicked), adikos (unrighteous, 1 Pet 3:18; Acts 24:15), asebes (ungodly, 1 Pet 4:18) and hamartolos (sinners, Matt 9:13, Mark 2:17, Luke 5:32, Rom 5:19). Those are different words. Reformed and Lutheran readers also care that 1 Pet 3:18 and Rom 5:19 (Christ the righteous for the unrighteous; the many 'made righteous') are here, where they read as a general moral contrast and not as a statement about Christ.
rows.fix: Relabel 'The righteous and their opposite (wicked, unrighteous, ungodly, sinners)'. Move Rom 5:19 and 1 Pet 3:18 to a small row 'One righteous for the many' with Isa 53:11, Rom 5:18-19, 2 Cor 5:21 and 1 Pet 3:18, so their placement is the text's and not a side effect of first-match.

rows.why: A 177-verse row that mixes God ('the LORD is righteous', Ps 145:17, Rev 16:5), Christ (Acts 3:14, 1 John 2:1), named people (Noah, Job, Cornelius, Zechariah and Elizabeth) and the denials (Rom 3:10, Eccl 7:20, Eccl 7:16). Under 'Called righteous' the denial verses read as the opposite of the label, which Reformed and Lutheran readers (Rom 3:10) and Wesleyan readers (1 John 3:7) will each read against their view. Naming Christ in the same list as Noah also runs into the project's rule that the divine persons are placed by hand.
rows.fix: Relabel 'Who is called righteous, and who is not'. Split into sub-rows 'God is righteous', 'The Righteous One (Christ)', 'People called righteous' and 'None is righteous' (Rom 3:10, Eccl 7:20, Ps 14:3 where the word occurs). The Christ row must be curated by hand.

rows.why: Because this row comes first, any verse with both faith and works lands here. James 2:24 ('justified by works and not by faith alone') is in this row and absent from the works row, which tilts toward the faith reading. Gal 2:16 and Rom 3:28 ('apart from works') are here too, so the works row has no Pauline denials. Two examples do not fit: Acts 13:38 (the text shown has no justification or faith in it; the justify verb is in 13:39) and 1 Tim 3:16 ('vindicated by the Spirit' is about Christ, not a believer's justification).
rows.fix: Add a row before these two, 'Justified, faith and works in one verse' (Rom 3:28, Rom 4:5, Gal 2:16, Jas 2:24), then keep the faith-only and works-only rows. Correct Acts 13:38 to Acts 13:39 and take 1 Tim 3:16 out. Keep the note as written.

rows.why: Matt 11:19 ('wisdom is vindicated by her actions') is a non-soteriological use of the same verb and the same word 'works', so it makes the row read as though 'justified by works' were a general claim. With the faith row ahead and taking Gal 2:16, Rom 3:28 and Jas 2:24, the remaining row is only Rom 3:20, 4:2 and James 2:21, 25, which makes James look like the exception and Paul like the rule.
rows.fix: Take Matt 11:19 out, move it to 'vindicated'. See the combined row suggested above to put Jas 2:24 and Gal 2:16 where both readers can see them.

rows.why: 'Vindicated' is a translator's choice, and this row holds the central soteriological verses (Rom 3:24, 5:9, 8:30, 1 Cor 6:11, Titus 3:7, Gal 5:4) with Judah's 'she is more righteous than I' and Luke 7:29. The label puts 'vindicated' on Rom 8:30 and 1 Cor 6:11, so Reformed and Lutheran readers will read it as downgrading a declaration, and Catholic and Orthodox readers will read it as ruling out 'made righteous'. Neither is intended, but the label is a verdict on the meaning of the verb.
rows.fix: Relabel with no verdict on the meaning, for instance 'Justified (faith and works not named in the verse)', or 'Justified: declared in the right, acquitted'. Keep Rom 3:24, 5:9, 8:30 as the lead examples so the main passages are visible.

misfits.why: The companion is 'judgment' (krima), and the verse contrasts condemnation with justification. It does not pair justice with righteousness. Acts 24:25 (judgment to come) is a weaker case.

misfits.row: The righteousness of the LORD, of God
misfits.why: 'Of God' here means 'children of God' and 'not from God'. The verse is about practising righteousness, not God's own righteousness.

misfits.row: The righteousness of the LORD, of God
misfits.why: These deny Israel's own righteousness; they say nothing about the righteousness of God.
Righteousness here is 'justice' in judging the world; 'faith' is the BSB's 'proof' (pistis, assurance). It has nothing to do with righteousness through faith.
'Persecuted because of righteousness' is neither seeking nor pursuing; the companion is only 'kingdom of heaven'.
'Pursuit' there is of evil. The righteousness half of the verse is about life.
Weak: the 'doing' is God's act of judging; the human practice of righteousness is not the subject.
The contrast is with 'wickedness' (anomia, rish'ah), not 'sin'.
The text shown has no justification or faith in it. The justified verb is in Acts 13:39, so the verse reference is off by one.
'Vindicated by the Spirit' is Christ's vindication; 'believed on in the world' is not about a person being justified by faith.
'Wisdom is vindicated by her actions' is not about a person's standing before God.

words: pistis as one of a list of virtues
different_words.verse: 1 Timothy 6:11; 2 Timothy 2:22 (same word, different use, not different words)

missing.what: The 'credited / counted as righteousness' wording, the text's own sensitive phrase, appears as no row of its own. It is scattered across the faith row, the 'of God' row and 'More', so a reader cannot see where the text says 'credited' beside where it says 'made' or 'became' (Rom 5:19, 2 Cor 5:21, Rom 6:18).

Verses on tsedeq (the noun Righteousness, 103 verses) look nearly absent: the noun section holds 237 verses against 345 across the five noun words, and none of the best-known tsedeq texts is in a row. Ps 89:14 is quoted at the top but is in no row.

Jesus on righteousness and righteousness as clothing, both left in 'More': 'fulfil all righteousness', 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the Pharisees', the robe of righteousness, the breastplate, the saints' righteous acts as fine linen.

summary: The labels are mostly neutral and the notes on the God row and the faith/works rows are balanced, but first-match ordering quietly decides where the contested verses sit (Jas 2:24, Gal 2:16 and Rom 1:17 are placed by the order and not by what they say) and several rows have an example or a companion word that is not what the label claims. Twelve of the eighteen rows need a change, mostly small (swap an example, relabel, or add a combined row for verses with two companions); the tsedeq noun verses and the 'credited' wording should be checked before the page goes public.
